analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְרָם אֶל לוֹט means “Abram said to Lot.” The name identifies Abram as the speaker.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It is the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְרָם אֶל לוֹט, “Abram said to Lot,” אֶל introduces Lot as the person Abram addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.

evidence.note: The genealogy lists Abram and Haran among Terah’s sons and names Lot as Haran’s son.
וְלוֹט עִמּוֹ names Lot as a companion of Abram on the journey from Egypt.

article.name: לוֹט
article.summary: Lot was the son of Haran, Abram’s brother. He accompanied Abram from Egypt toward the Negeb. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לוֹט. The derivation of the name is uncertain.
draft.definition: Lot, son of Haran and nephew of Abram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:27 names Haran as Lot’s father. Genesis 13:1 names Lot as Abram’s companion on the journey from Egypt.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אַבְרָם אֶל לוֹט, “Abram said to Lot,” אֶל introduces Lot as the addressee. Abram appeals to their kinship with כִּי אֲנָשִׁים אַחִים אֲנָחְנוּ, “for we are kinsmen.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אַל נָא תְהִי מְרִיבָה, נָא marks Abram’s plea, and מְרִיבָה is the subject of תְהִי. Abram asks Lot, “Please, let there be no quarrel between me and you.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew negative particle with no prefix or suffix. It negates the third-person feminine singular jussive תְהִי.

analysis.evidence: In אַל נָא תְהִי מְרִיבָה, אַל negates the jussive תְהִי, and נָא softens Abram’s appeal to Lot: “Please let there be no quarrel between me and you.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew particle of entreaty, with no prefix or suffix.
